name: Priya Venkataraman
title: Marine Biologist & Ocean Conservation Lead
about: I study the intersection of coral reef ecology and climate science, working to understand and protect the ocean ecosystems most threatened by a warming world. With fieldwork across the Indo-Pacific and the Caribbean, I bring both laboratory precision and deep-sea curiosity to every project I take on.
summary: Award-winning marine biologist with 10 years of field and laboratory research experience across Indo-Pacific reef systems. Led multi-institutional coral resilience studies and authored 14 peer-reviewed publications on ocean warming impacts. Passionate about translating complex ecological data into actionable conservation policy. Recipient of the 2023 Pew Marine Fellowship.

experience.company: Australian Institute of Marine Science — Townsville, QLD
experience.description: Lead a 12-person research team investigating thermal bleaching thresholds across the Great Barrier Reef. Secured AUD 3.2M in competitive research grants. Developed a predictive bleaching model adopted by the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Authority for annual reef health reports.

Conducted baseline biodiversity surveys across 40+ reef sites in the Coral Triangle. Trained 25 local conservation officers in eDNA sampling and underwater photographic survey methods. Published findings in Nature Climate Change and Marine Ecology Progress Series.

Investigated symbiodinium shuffling in bleached Acropora corals under laboratory temperature stress conditions. Co-authored 5 peer-reviewed papers during PhD candidature. Awarded university medal for best doctoral thesis in biological sciences.
